items_missed: No explicit agenda-setting statement ("I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes") and no explicit "sound good?" confirmation before diving into discovery
Didn't explicitly check that the August 8th date still worked before jumping into address/home details — treated it as already locked from the quote form
Didn't ask about stairs or where items are located floor-to-floor beyond noting each property is two-story
Didn't ask about storage needs or the moving-stressors question ("is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?")
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000 for accidental damage)
Never mentioned Meet Your Mover (photo + basic info emailed before the move)
Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee (discounting if the crew misses the arrival window)
Didn't give packing-service pricing when Roy asked for help with TV/furniture prep beyond what's included in the hourly rate
No concrete equivalent/comparison used to make the time or box estimate tangible (e.g., a size reference for ~80 boxes)
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips, no "take a carload" tip, no mention that prep before move day shortens the job and lowers the bill
Didn't explicitly state that no deposit is required to book
Didn't ask Roy to reply with any corrections to verify the emailed details, and didn't give branch hours or the best way to reach the office
Only used the customer's name once, at the very opening ("Hi, Roy") — never used it again across the rest of the call
No insurance explanation (No Worries coverage + 60 cents/lb baseline liability) and no genuine rapport/humor moment — tone stayed transactional throughout
top_strength: Grant ran a thorough, well-organized discovery — parking access at both ends, garage/backyard contents, packing readiness, and a box-count check — and delivered a clear, specific estimate (3-man crew, one truck, 7.5-8.5 hours, up to $2,779.50) with a clean explanation of the hourly clock and minimum.
coaching_note: The single highest-leverage fix is that Grant skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely (0/10) on a move he himself estimated at ~80 boxes — walking Roy through consolidation tips and the "take a carload" trick right after the pricing explanation could visibly shave hours (and the top end of that $2,779.50 estimate) and should become a standard close to every pricing conversation.
phone_presence_notes: Grant was polite and cooperative with frequent casual acknowledgments ("gotcha," "good deal," "alrighty"), but the delivery was list-like and transactional, and he never used the customer's name again after the opening greeting.
